source.method: 7 parallel subsystem auditors + 7 adversarial verifiers over the real codebase

headline_findings: ROOT CAUSE 1 — every scan is rejected: performOcr reads a tesseract.js field that does not exist, so OCR confidence is always 0 and runOcrWithRetry rejects the document (packages/api/src/services/ocr.ts).

ROOT CAUSE 2 — every real image is rejected in transport: the live Express scan service mounts express.json() with body-parser's 100kb default while the caller POSTs the whole image as JSON (packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/index.js:19).

ROOT CAUSE 3 — the UI can never show success: useFileUpload computes completion from a stale closure, so stage never leaves 'uploading' and UploadComplete/UploadError are unreachable (apps/nextjs/src/hooks/use-file-upload.ts:169-172).
Camera capture on /scan writes to state and is never uploaded; a working camera->upload implementation exists but is orphaned in upload-form.tsx.

ZERO-STORAGE VIOLATIONS on the live path: uploaded medical images are written to disk (gemini-scan-backend/src/routes/scan.js:65,81) and extracted PHI is written as JSON (:99), readable over an unauthenticated GET.
No consent gate exists anywhere: MedicalDisclaimerOverlay and useMedicalDisclaimer are fully written and rendered by nothing, and the copy cites HIPAA rather than RA 10173.
PHI is never scrubbed on the live scan path: scanGuestImage sends the raw image and raw OCR text to a third party, while phiScrubber sits wired only into orphaned code.
Dialect auto-detection by geography does not exist: dialectDetection.ts detects from text and has zero callers; navigator.geolocation is used only by the facilities map.
Two Express AI services exist. The product-required one (ai-sidecar, LangChain/LangGraph, 1661 LOC) is 100% orphaned; the one that runs is plain JS, outside every quality gate, and domain-wrong.
imagePreprocessor implements real deskew/denoise/binarize but dynamically imports 'canvas', which is not a dependency, so it logs 'preprocessing disabled' and no-ops at runtime.
The medical parsing engine is 4 generic layout regexes plus a 70-entry alias table and 21 reference ranges — far short of the 200+ Philippine test variants the product requires.
The rich results UI (SeverityIndicator, ConfidenceScore, PlainLanguageSummary, TanongMoCard) renders only on /documents/[id], the authenticated DB-persisted route, and never on /scan.
scanGuestImage is a publicProcedure with no auth, no rate limit and no payload cap, and base64Image has no maximum size.
Tests are partly theatre: hooks/__tests__/use-file-upload.test.ts never imports useFileUpload, and the router and AI integration suites are excluded from CI.

conventions.commit_style: one-line conventional commit, lowercase, max 120 chars; '+' joins distinct changes, '&' joins correlated details (.agents/rules/git-policy.md)
conventions.verify_command: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test

compliance_invariants: Medical documents, their bytes, their OCR text and extracted PHI are never written to a database, object store, Cloudinary or disk.
phiScrubber runs before any outbound third-party LLM call.
The audit trail records actions and metadata, never medical content.
No file may be read before Terms of Service, Terms & Conditions and the medical disclaimer are accepted.
Secrets come only from environment variables declared in turbo.json.
The UI always carries the not-medical-advice disclaimer and never presents AI output as diagnosis.

epics.goal: No medical document, image, OCR text, or extracted PHI is persisted anywhere, and no upload can begin before Terms of Service, Terms & Conditions and the medical disclaimer are affirmatively accepted.

tasks.description:
Generate a per-request scanId instead of the constant 'unknown'. In packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/routes/scan.js:43 replace `const scanId = sanitizePathSegment(metadata.requestId) || uuidv4();` with a form that only accepts a real client id: `const rawId = typeof metadata.requestId === 'string' && metadata.requestId.trim() ? sanitizePathSegment(metadata.requestId) : null; const scanId = rawId ?? uuidv4();`. Separately, in packages/api/src/router/documents.ts add `requestId: crypto.randomUUID()` to the metadata object sent at lines 768-777 so every request from Next.js carries a correlatable id, and thread that value through to the requestId returned by normalizeGuestScanResponse.

ALSO (VALID): Sidecar assigns every scan the literal scanId "unknown", so all patients share one storage directory and one result file behind the unauthenticated GET — packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/routes/scan.js:43 is `const scanId = sanitizePathSegment(metadata.requestId) || uuidv4();`. sanitizePathSegment (scan.js:20-23) returns the string 'unknown' for any non-string input, and 'unknown' is truthy, so the uuidv4() fallback is unreachable dead code. packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:756-766 never sends metadata.requestId. Consequence: every guest image is written to data/uploads/unknown/<filename> (storage.js:33-36) — two users uploading IMG_0001.jpg silently overwrite each other's medical document — and every AI result overwrites data/results/unknown.json (db.js:27-28). The unauthenticated GET /api/scan/:scanId (scan.js:108-113) therefore has a single well-known id: any caller fetching /api/scan/unknown receives the most recent patient's full medical analysis.
FIX: Fix is subsumed by removing persistence entirely (the audit's sidecar task). If persistence is retained in any interim commit, generate scanId server-side with uuidv4() unconditionally and never derive it from request metadata, and delete the GET handler at scan.js:108-113.

ALSO (EXTRACT): Every live guest scan is written under the same scanId 'unknown', so images and result JSON overwrite each other and an unauthenticated GET returns the last user's PHI — packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/routes/scan.js:43 `const scanId = sanitizePathSegment(metadata.requestId) || uuidv4();`. sanitizePathSegment (scan.js:20-23) returns the string 'unknown' for a non-string input, which is truthy, so the `|| uuidv4()` branch is unreachable. packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:757-766 never sends `requestId` in metadata, so metadata.requestId is always undefined on the live path. Result: every scan writes to data/uploads/unknown/<filename> (storage.js:33-36) and data/results/unknown.json (db.js:27-28), each request clobbering the previous user's file, and GET /api/scan/unknown (scan.js:108-113) returns the most recent user's complete extracted PHI with no authentication. The filename collides too — documents.ts:754 sends an optional fileName, and scan.js:65 falls back through the same sanitizePathSegment to 'unknown'.
FIX: This is subsumed by removing persistence entirely (the audit's task 1), but if any id is kept, fix scan.js:43 to `const scanId = (typeof metadata.requestId === 'string' && metadata.requestId.trim()) ? sanitizePathSegment(metadata.requestId) : uuidv4();` and add a test asserting two consecutive requests without requestId receive distinct ids.

Remove Cloudinary persistence of medical documents from the Next.js scan route. apps/nextjs/src/app/api/documents/scan/route.ts:99-133 uploads the raw medical image/PDF to Cloudinary (folder 'klaro/scan') and writes the resulting secure_url into document.storageUrl — a direct RA 10173 zero-storage violation — while its own docstring at :36-37 falsely claims the route 'triggers OCR processing' (no OCR call exists in the file; its imports at :3-15 include no @klaro/api service). Delete the cloudinary.config block (:17-21), the upload_stream promise (:99-115) and the cloudinaryUrl handling (:117-121); remove storageUrl from the document insert at :130. Replace the route body with an in-memory hand-off: decode the file to a Buffer and call the OCR pipeline directly (or return 501 and point clients at documents.scanGuestImage) so no medical bytes ever leave the request. Apply the same removal to the storageUrl field in packages/api/src/router/documents.ts upload (:178-230, storageUrl at :202).

ALSO (SCANUI): COMPLIANCE VIOLATION: /api/documents/scan uploads the medical document to Cloudinary and persists it to the DB — apps/nextjs/src/app/api/documents/scan/route.ts is a live App Router endpoint inside the very scan surface this audit covers, and the auditor never listed it. It accepts multipart 'file' (:58-59), buffers the whole document (:96-97), streams it to Cloudinary under `folder: "klaro/scan"` (:99-115), then inserts a `document` row carrying `storageUrl: cloudinaryUrl`, `fileName`, `mimeType`, `fileSize` (:123-133) plus an `analysis` row (:139-146). This is exactly the ZERO-STORAGE prohibition. The sibling apps/nextjs/src/app/api/uploads/server/route.ts:16-20,99-118 does the same. Both are unreferenced by any client code (`grep -rn "api/documents/scan|api/uploads" apps/nextjs/src | grep -v "app/api/"` -> zero hits), but an unused route file still deploys as a public HTTP endpoint — and GET /api/documents/scan (:176-198) advertises the upload contract to anyone. `cloudinary` is a real dependency (apps/nextjs/package.json:32), so this code runs.
FIX: Delete apps/nextjs/src/app/api/documents/scan/route.ts and apps/nextjs/src/app/api/uploads/server/route.ts (plus /api/uploads/sign and /api/uploads/[id] after checking their callers), drop `cloudinary` from apps/nextjs/package.json, and add a CI grep guard asserting no `cloudinary.uploader` / `storageUrl` write exists under apps/nextjs/src. If a document record must exist for audit purposes, store only a non-reversible hash and metadata, never the file or a retrievable URL.

ALSO (VALID): Stop persisting medical documents to Cloudinary and stop storing plaintext OCR text — Remove the cloudinary.uploader.upload_stream block at apps/nextjs/src/app/api/documents/scan/route.ts:99-121 and the equivalent at apps/nextjs/src/app/api/uploads/server/route.ts:104, and stop writing storageUrl (scan/route.ts:130, uploads/server/route.ts:130). Pass the buffer straight to the processing pipeline instead. Stop writing plaintext ocrText at packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:279 and :585. Then drop the ocr_text and storage_url columns from packages/db/src/schema.ts:70,72 with a migration, and update services/documentService.ts and services/fileCleanup.ts, which read them.

ALSO (DATA): Delete the orphaned Cloudinary upload and document-read REST routes — Delete the four unreferenced route files that persist medical documents: apps/nextjs/src/app/api/documents/scan/route.ts, apps/nextjs/src/app/api/uploads/server/route.ts, apps/nextjs/src/app/api/uploads/sign/route.ts and apps/nextjs/src/app/api/uploads/[id]/route.ts, together with their sibling test files apps/nextjs/src/app/api/documents/scan/__tests__/route.test.ts and the upload sections of apps/nextjs/src/app/api/__tests__/auth.integration.test.ts. None has a non-test caller (verified by grep), but each is a live public endpoint that writes medical bytes to Cloudinary and PHI to Postgres. Also remove the now-unused '/api/documents/scan' and '/api/uploads' assertions in packages/api/src/__tests__/openapi.test.ts:29 and any OpenAPI spec entries that describe them.

tasks.description:
Raise the sidecar JSON body limit to match its declared image budget. In packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/index.js:19 change `app.use(express.json())` to `app.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }))`. The 100kb body-parser default currently rejects every real photograph before routes/scan.js runs, which makes documents.ts:770-776 fall through to buildFallbackGuestScanResult. 15mb accommodates the 10MB MAX_BASE64_SIZE declared at routes/scan.js:18 plus base64 overhead.

ALSO (SIDECAR): BLOCKER: express.json()'s 100kb default body limit makes the entire live guest-scan path fail for any real medical image — packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/index.js:19 `app.use(express.json());` — no `limit` option, so body-parser's 100kb default applies. The only production caller sends the full image inline as JSON: packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:750-756 `body: JSON.stringify({ images: [{ bytesBase64: input.base64Image, ... }] ...})`. apps/nextjs/src/lib/file-validation.ts:14 allows files up to `50 * 1024 * 1024`, and packages/validators/src/scan-analysis.ts:35-43 puts no `.max()` on base64Image. A 100kb JSON envelope caps the image at roughly 75KB of raw bytes — smaller than any phone photo. Express throws PayloadTooLargeError before the route, index.js registers no error handler, so the client gets a 413 HTML page; documents.ts:770-776 turns that into `buildFallbackGuestScanResult`, which documents.ts:86 stamps `status: "completed"` and :97 `confidence: 0.6`. The service's own test masks it — packages/gemini-scan-backend/tests/scan.jsonbody.test.js:7 uses `Buffer.alloc(100,'x').toString('base64')` (136 bytes). Net effect: the AI integration the whole product depends on has never worked end-to-end with a real document, and it fails silently as a confident-looking medical result.
FIX: Set an explicit limit that matches the documented contract, e.g. `app.use(express.json({ limit: '15mb' }))` in packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/index.js:19 (or on the /api/scan route only), and add an Express error handler that maps `err.type === 'entity.too.large'` to a 413 JSON body `{error:'file_too_large'}`. Add `.max()` to base64ImageSchema in packages/validators/src/scan-analysis.ts:35-43 so oversized payloads are rejected at the tRPC edge with a real message instead of being swallowed into a fabricated 'completed' result. Add a regression test that posts a >1MB base64 payload and asserts a 200 (or an explicit 413 JSON error), not the fallback.

ALSO (EXTRACT): The live guest scan can never succeed with a real image: the Express service is mounted with express.json()'s default 100kb body limit — packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/index.js:19 `app.use(express.json());` with no limit option; express ^4.21.2 (packages/gemini-scan-backend/package.json) uses body-parser's 100kb default. packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:746-768 POSTs `Content-Type: application/json` carrying the entire `bytesBase64` image (documents.ts:753). A 1MB photo becomes ~1.37MB of base64, so body-parser returns 413 before routes/scan.js:32 executes; documents.ts:770-776 then returns buildFallbackGuestScanResult with status 'completed' and the fabricated 0.6 confidence. The whole /api/scan handler including its own MAX_BASE64_SIZE guard (scan.js:18, :61) is dead code for real inputs. Tests never catch it: tests/scan.jsonbody.test.js:7 posts `Buffer.alloc(100,'x').toString('base64')` and tests/fixtures/sample.jpg is 20 bytes. capturePhoto (upload-form.tsx:309) makes it worse by encoding a 1280x720 frame as PNG.
FIX: In packages/gemini-scan-backend/src/index.js:19, replace `express.json()` with `express.json({ limit: '15mb' })` to match the route's own MAX_FILE_SIZE/MAX_BASE64_SIZE of 10MB plus base64 overhead, and add an error handler that converts body-parser's PayloadTooLargeError into the route's `{error:'file_too_large'}` JSON shape instead of Express's default HTML page. Add a regression test that posts a >1MB base64 image and asserts a 200 (or a JSON 413), not an HTML error.

tasks.description:
Fix the stale-closure completion check in useFileUpload so stage reaches complete/error. In apps/nextjs/src/hooks/use-file-upload.ts, delete the `queue.concat(newItems)` computation at lines 169-172. Have processFile return a per-file outcome (e.g. change its signature to `Promise<'complete' | 'error' | 'cancelled'>` and return the matching literal from the success path at :117-119, the result.status==='error' path at :104, the catch at :134, and the three cancellation early-returns at :62, :73, :90). In upload(), collect the returned outcomes from the sequential loop at :163-166 into a local array and derive the final state from that array only: if any outcome is 'error' -> setStage('error') + setError('Some files failed to upload.'); else if every non-cancelled outcome is 'complete' -> setStage('complete') + setProgress(100). Remove `queue` from the useCallback dependency array at :182 so upload() is no longer recreated on every queue mutation. Also drive the top-level progress from the per-file outcomes: after each processFile resolves, setProgress(Math.round((index + 1) / newItems.length * 100)) instead of leaving it pinned at the 10 set at :159.

ALSO (SIDECAR): Stale-closure bug in useFileUpload: the upload flow never reaches the 'complete' stage — apps/nextjs/src/hooks/use-file-upload.ts:169-172 computes `const allComplete = queue.concat(newItems).every(f => f.stage === 'complete' || cancelledRef.current.has(f.id));` and `const anyError = queue.concat(newItems).some(f => f.stage === 'error');`. Both read `queue` captured in the `useCallback` closure at line 182 (`[processFile, onError, queue]`) — i.e. the queue as it was BEFORE `setQueue((prev) => [...prev, ...newItems])` at line 157. Worse, `newItems` are the literal objects created at lines 150-155 with `stage: 'pending'`, and `processFile` never mutates them: every update goes through `setQueue(prev => prev.map(...))` (lines 65-69, 75-79, 106-117, 122-133), producing new objects. So after a fully successful upload `allComplete` is false and `anyError` is false, neither branch at lines 174-180 fires, and `stage` stays `'uploading'` with `progress` stuck at 10 forever. A second, related bug: `cancelFile` (lines 208-215) resets a cancelled file's stage to `'pending'`, which `isUploading` (lines 233-238) counts as in-flight, so cancelling also pins the UI in the uploading state permanently.
FIX: Have `processFile` return its terminal outcome (or accumulate results in a local array inside `upload`) and derive `allComplete`/`anyError` from that local value rather than from the captured `queue`. Alternatively read the latest queue via a ref (`queueRef.current`) updated in a `useEffect`, and drop `queue` from the `useCallback` deps. Separately, give cancelled items a distinct `'cancelled'` stage instead of `'pending'` at line 212 and exclude it from `isUploading` at lines 233-238.

ALSO (OCR): Stale-closure bug in useFileUpload: the upload never reaches a terminal stage — apps/nextjs/src/hooks/use-file-upload.ts:169-180. tasks.description:
Release the camera MediaStream on unmount and on late getUserMedia resolution. apps/nextjs/src/layouts/SampleScanner/ScannerUI.tsx:102-110 reads `const video = videoRef.current;` in the effect body with `[]` deps, so it executes once at mount. At mount `isScanning` is false (:56), so `scannerPreview` is null (:247) and the `<video ref={videoRef}>` element (:250) is NOT in the tree — `videoRef.current` is null. The cleanup closure therefore holds `video === null`, `video?.srcObject` is undefined, and `stream.getTracks().forEach(track => track.stop())` (:107) never runs. Only handleCancelScan (:135-144) and handleCapture (:157) stop tracks. Navigating away or unmounting while the camera preview is open leaves getUserMedia's stream running. The auditor not only missed this, its recommended task asserts "The camera MediaStream cleanup at :102-110 continues to work unchanged".

FIX: Hold the stream in a ref (`streamRef.current = stream` in startCamera, ScannerUI.tsx:120) and stop every track in an unmount cleanup that reads `streamRef.current` at teardown time — not a mount-time snapshot of videoRef.current. Also stop the stream immediately in startCamera's success path if `videoRef.current` is null when getUserMedia resolves (:121), which currently drops the stream with no reference to release.

ALSO (DATA): Camera MediaStream leaks when the upload form unmounts while getUserMedia is still pending — apps/nextjs/src/components/upload-form.tsx:163-169 awaits navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia, then at :170 `if (!mounted) return;` bails out BEFORE assigning the stream to videoRef.current.srcObject (:172). The effect's cleanup at :182-191 stops tracks only via `videoRef.current.srcObject instanceof MediaStream`, so a stream resolved after unmount is never reachable and `stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())` is never called — the camera stays live (indicator on) for the life of the tab. Same class of bug is absent in ScannerUI.tsx, which stops tracks at :107 and :138.
FIX: Hold the stream in a ref assigned immediately after the await, and in the `!mounted` branch call `stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())` before returning; have the cleanup stop the ref'd stream rather than reading it back off the video element.

ALSO (VALID): Camera MediaStream leaks whenever getUserMedia resolves after unmount or before the video element exists — apps/nextjs/src/components/upload-form.tsx:158-193. startCamera awaits navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia at :163-169. At :170 `if (!mounted) return;` discards the resolved stream without calling stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()). At :171 the stream is only retained if videoRef.current is non-null — otherwise it falls through with no cleanup. The unmount cleanup at :183-192 can only stop a stream already attached to videoRef.current.srcObject, so in both cases the tracks stay live and the device camera indicator stays on after the user leaves the page. React 18 StrictMode's dev double-mount triggers this on every load.
FIX: Hold the acquired stream in a ref (or a local variable checked by the cleanup) and stop its tracks in both early-return branches: `if (!mounted || !videoRef.current) { stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()); return; }`, and have the cleanup stop the ref'd stream rather than reading videoRef.current.srcObject.

ALSO (OCR): Camera MediaStream leaks when getUserMedia resolves after unmount (React StrictMode double-invoke hits this every dev mount) — apps/nextjs/src/components/upload-form.tsx:158-193. The effect calls `void startCamera()` at :182 and returns a cleanup at :183-192 that stops tracks ONLY via `videoRef.current.srcObject`. If the effect is torn down before `await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia(...)` at :163-169 resolves, cleanup runs while `videoRef.current.srcObject` is still null and stops nothing; the promise then resolves, hits `if (!mounted) return;` at :170 and drops the live `stream` on the floor WITHOUT calling `stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())`. The same leak occurs if `videoRef.current` is null at :171 — the stream is neither attached nor stopped. The user's camera stays on with the hardware indicator lit and no UI attached to it. This is both a resource leak and a privacy problem on a medical-document app.
FIX: Hold the stream in a ref as soon as it resolves and stop it from a single place: `const s = await getUserMedia(...); streamRef.current = s; if (!mounted) { s.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()); return; }` and have the cleanup stop `streamRef.current` rather than reading it back off the video element.

ALSO (EXTRACT): Camera stream is acquired but the preview can never mount and the stream is never released, leaving the device camera held open — apps/nextjs/src/components/upload-form.tsx:72 initialises `cameraActive` to false. The `<video ref={videoRef}>` at :388-393 is rendered only inside `{cameraActive ? ... }` at :386, so on mount videoRef.current is null. The mount effect at :158-193 calls getUserMedia at :163, then guards `if (videoRef.current)` at :171 before ever calling setCameraActive(true) at :174 — a guard that can never pass on first mount. The result is that the preview never appears (the user always sees the 'camera not available' placeholder at :437), capturePhoto at :297-298 always early-returns, and the acquired MediaStream is never assigned anywhere. The cleanup at :183-192 can only stop tracks reachable through videoRef.current.srcObject, so it stops nothing — the camera stays acquired (indicator light on) for the life of the page. The `if (!mounted) return;` at :170 is a second leak path for the same reason. Note apps/nextjs/src/components/upload-form.tsx is excluded from coverage thresholds at vitest.config.ts.
FIX: Hold the stream in a ref (`streamRef.current = stream`) before the videoRef guard, call setCameraActive(true) unconditionally on success, render the `<video>` element unconditionally (hide it with CSS when inactive) so the ref is populated, attach srcObject in a follow-up effect keyed on cameraActive, and have the cleanup stop `streamRef.current.getTracks()` rather than reading through videoRef. Also stop the tracks in the `!mounted` early-return branch.

ALSO (SIDECAR): Camera MediaStream is leaked when the component unmounts mid-getUserMedia or the video ref is null — apps/nextjs/src/components/upload-form.tsx:163-175: the stream is acquired at line 163, then `if (!mounted) return;` at line 170 returns WITHOUT calling `stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop())`, and `if (videoRef.current)` at line 171 skips attachment entirely when the ref is null. The cleanup at lines 183-192 only stops tracks it can reach through `videoRef.current.srcObject`, so in both of those paths the camera stays open for the life of the tab (recording indicator on, device held). This is the classic async-acquire/sync-cleanup race: `getUserMedia` resolves after the effect's cleanup has already run.
FIX: Capture the stream in a variable visible to the cleanup (e.g. `let activeStream: MediaStream | null = null;` in the effect body, assigned right after `await getUserMedia`), stop it immediately in the `!mounted` branch at line 170 and in the `videoRef.current == null` case, and have the cleanup at lines 183-192 stop `activeStream` as well as `videoRef.current.srcObject`.

ALSO (CLARA): Camera MediaStream is never stopped on unmount (stale ref captured at mount) and can leak entirely on a fast permission grant — apps/nextjs/src/layouts/SampleScanner/ScannerUI.tsx:102-110 is `useEffect(() => { const video = videoRef.current; return () => { const stream = video?.srcObject; ... stop() } }, [])` — it captures videoRef.current ONCE at mount. The <video ref={videoRef}> element only renders when isScanning is true (ScannerUI.tsx:247-249 `if (isScanning) { scannerPreview = (<video ref={videoRef} .../>) }`), and isScanning initialises to false (:56). So `video` is always null and the cleanup is a no-op: navigating away mid-scan leaves the camera track live and the hardware indicator on. Second defect on the same path: handleStartScan (:130-133) does setIsScanning(true) then `await startCamera()`; if the permission is already granted getUserMedia can resolve before React commits the <video>, so the `if (videoRef.current)` guard at :121 fails and the acquired stream is neither attached nor stopped — an unrecoverable leak with no reference left to it. This path is reachable from the chat composer (ChatInput onCameraClick, ScannerUI.tsx:715).
FIX: Read the ref inside the cleanup instead of the effect body: `return () => { const s = videoRef.current?.srcObject; if (s instanceof MediaStream) s.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()); }`, and hold the stream in a ref (streamRef.current = stream) inside startCamera before the videoRef guard at :121 so a stream acquired before commit is still stoppable. Acceptance: unmounting ScannerUI while isScanning stops all tracks; granting permission instantly still attaches or stops the stream.

tasks.description:
Terminate the sidecar Tesseract worker in a finally block. packages/ai-sidecar/src/shared/ocr.ts:42-49: `const worker = await createWorker('eng'); const { data } = await worker.recognize(preprocessed); await worker.terminate();` — there is no try/finally, so any throw from `worker.recognize()` (corrupt image, OOM, unsupported format) skips `terminate()` and orphans the tesseract worker process and its ~30MB language data for the life of the node process. `preprocessImage` at line 39 can also throw before the worker exists, but the reverse ordering means a sharp failure inside `recognize` leaves the worker hanging. tasks.description:
Abort the SSE chat stream on client disconnect and keep PHI out of the query string. packages/ai-sidecar/src/routes/chat-stream.ts:61-96 iterates `retrievalGraph.streamEvents(...)` with no `signal` and registers no `req.on('close', ...)` handler. epics.title: Security, authorization and the compliance audit trail
epics.goal: Every public procedure is rate limited and size bounded, admin surfaces are gated, and every scan, OCR and chat action writes a redacted audit record carrying no raw PHI.

tasks.description:
Add a rate-limited public procedure and apply it to scanGuestImage. In packages/api/src/trpc.ts add `guestScanProcedure` built as `t.procedure.use(timingMiddleware).use(...)` — the same limiter body as scanProcedure (trpc.ts:176-189) but WITHOUT authMiddleware, keying on `ctx.session?.user?.id ?? ctx.ipAddress ?? 'anon'` since ctx.ipAddress already exists (trpc.ts:49-52). Then change packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:729 from publicProcedure to guestScanProcedure. Also add `.max()` to base64ImageSchema in packages/validators/src/scan-analysis.ts:35-43 — cap the base64 string at roughly 14_000_000 chars (~10MB decoded) to match the sidecar's MAX_BASE64_SIZE.

ALSO (SCANUI): documents.scanGuestImage is a publicProcedure with no auth and no rate limit — while a rate-limited scanProcedure exists and is used elsewhere — packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:729 declares `scanGuestImage: publicProcedure`, and packages/api/src/trpc.ts:132 defines `publicProcedure = t.procedure.use(timingMiddleware)` — timing only, no auth, no throttle. A purpose-built `scanProcedure` with `checkRateLimit(`scan:${userId}`, 10)` exists at packages/api/src/trpc.ts:176-181 and is applied to `upload` (documents.ts:178), `processServerOcr` (:552) and `generateAnalysis` (:615) — but NOT to the one procedure the entire /scan and /scan/guest UI calls (use-file-upload.ts:81 and app/scan/guest/page.tsx:65). scanGuestInputSchema (packages/validators/src/scan-analysis.ts:45-52) is the only gate. Every accepted call performs OCR (documents.ts:739) and a paid Gemini POST (:746-768).
FIX: Add an IP/fingerprint-keyed rate limit middleware to scanGuestImage (the app already has apps/nextjs/src/lib/rate-limit.ts checkRateLimit used at api/documents/scan/route.ts:44-52), and enforce a hard byte cap on base64Image in scanGuestInputSchema rather than relying on the browser-side 50MB check in file-validation.ts:14.

ALSO (DATA): The live guest scan endpoint is an unauthenticated, unrate-limited, unbounded-payload OCR + Gemini proxy — packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:729 `scanGuestImage: publicProcedure` — publicProcedure is only `t.procedure.use(timingMiddleware)` (packages/api/src/trpc.ts:132), while a rate-limited `scanProcedure` exists at trpc.ts:176 and is used by upload (:178) and processServerOcr (:552). The input's base64ImageSchema (packages/validators/src/scan-analysis.ts:34-42) has `.min(100)` and NO `.max()`, so an anonymous caller can post an arbitrarily large base64 blob that is decoded (ocrPipeline.ts:30), run through tesseract (services/ocr.ts:113-114) and forwarded to the Gemini sidecar (documents.ts:746-768). This is the primary shipped product path (upload-form.tsx:81, scan/guest/page.tsx:25). Two sibling public LLM endpoints have the same problem: root.ts:32-43 `llmTest` is a publicProcedure that forwards an arbitrary 2000-char prompt to callLLMAPI and returns the model output verbatim, and documents.ts:805 `analyzeScanWithAI` is a publicProcedure that reaches the LLM and is live-wired from ScanAgentSidebar.tsx:58.
FIX: Add an IP/session-keyed rate-limit middleware for public procedures (reuse packages/api/src/middleware/rateLimiter.ts, already imported at trpc.ts:18) and apply it to scanGuestImage, analyzeScanWithAI and llmTest; add a `.max()` to base64ImageSchema sized to the 50MB file cap; and delete llmTest, which is a debug endpoint with no product purpose.

ALSO (OCR): The only live OCR endpoint is unauthenticated, unthrottled, and served with wildcard CORS — packages/api/src/router/documents.ts:729 `scanGuestImage: publicProcedure`. packages/api/src/trpc.ts:132 defines `publicProcedure = t.procedure.use(timingMiddleware)` — timing only, no auth, no rate limit. Every OTHER scan-family endpoint in the same router uses `scanProcedure` (trpc.ts:176-189: authMiddleware + `checkRateLimit(\`scan:${userId}\`, 10)`) — upload:178, processServerOcr:552, generateAnalysis:615 — yet the one procedure that actually runs OCR and calls an external AI backend has neither. On top of that, apps/nextjs/src/app/api/trpc/[trpc]/route.ts:12-17 sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: "*"` plus `Allow-Methods: OPTIONS, GET, POST` on every tRPC response, so any origin can invoke it cross-site. Each call spawns up to three Tesseract workers (ocrPipeline.ts:91 plus the loop at :108-147, each doing a full `createWorker("eng")` + `terminate()` cycle at ocr.ts:113-144) and then issues a 30s outbound fetch (documents.ts:746-749). This is unauthenticated CPU/memory/egress amplification against a medical endpoint. The audit reports the flags and the OCR bug but never checks the procedure type on the single live entry point.
FIX: Introduce a guest-scoped rate-limited procedure in packages/api/src/trpc.ts (IP-keyed via ctx.headers x-forwarded-for, the same key shape apps/nextjs/src/app/api/documents/scan/route.ts:44-48 already uses) and change documents.ts:729 from publicProcedure to it. tasks.description: The pre-commit hook is broken by construction and blocks every commit when core.hooksPath points at .husky. .husky/pre-commit sources .husky/_/husky.sh and runs `pnpm lint-staged`, but: (a) `husky` is not declared in any package.json, (b) `lint-staged` is not declared in any package.json, (c) there is no `prepare` script so husky never generates the .husky/_ bootstrap directory, and (d) there is no lint-staged configuration anywhere. Verified with `grep -rn '"husky"|"lint-staged"' --include=package.json .` which returns nothing. Either repair it properly — add husky and lint-staged as root devDependencies, add `"prepare": "husky"` to the root package.json scripts, and add a lint-staged config running prettier --write and eslint --fix on staged ts/tsx files — or delete .husky/pre-commit so the repo stops shipping a hook that cannot run.
tasks.rationale: Verified directly during this audit: a fresh clone plus install cannot satisfy this hook, so every contributor must pass --no-verify. A quality gate that everyone bypasses is worse than no gate.

grep for 'lint-staged' in package.json returns a declared dependency and a config block
